newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: World Bank calls for Slovak independent mkt body.
newsitem.headline: World Bank calls for Slovak independent mkt body.

text.p: Slovakia should establish an independent capital market supervision body to gain investor confidence, the World Bank (WB) said in a report.
"A regulatory body would concentrate on the authorisation, supervision, and, if neccessary, sanctioning of issuers, investors and intermediaries," the bank said.
The report said much of Slovak capital market regulation was left to the administrative discretion of the ministry of finance and had no transparent standards or criteria for decision-making.

"The creation of an independent securities commision would ensure transparency, improve efficiency and credibility of financial markets, and contribute to the elimination of administrative discretion in the regulation of capital markets," the WB said.
The report said that Slovakia should also rationalise its equity market to allow de-listing and de-registration of the non-liquid and smaller stocks "in well-defined cases".
At the end of 1995, 19 issues were listed on the Bratislava Stock Exchange while an additional 790 equities were registered on both the BSE and the over-the-counter RMS.

Amendments to the securities law in August brought registration of some 288 new shares after it had curbed trades in non-organised markets, the report said adding it is doubdtful that all of the benefit from direct access to the capital market.
"A major part of these registered or listed companies... would benefit from transforming their corporate form and continue their operations as privately held limited liability companies," it said.

The report added that the rationalisation of the equity markets, taking into account protection of the interests of minority shareholders, would significantly reduce the number of stocks to a core of companies that meet listing standards.
